name: SimOps
tagline: Design, simulate, and compare process pipelines.
description: Agent-led process modelling: interview to design, edit to compose, run to forecast. Built on the SimOps engine (ProcessConfig, cascade, predictor, optimizer) and the Fermi forecasting layer.

schema_json.description: Action grammar for the SimOps companion agent. Every structured action the companion emits — and every typed API call or CLI command — conforms to one of these six types.

canonical_document.description: The process pipeline — stages, efficiencies, sidestreams, SOSA contracts.

action_types.description: Patch the canonical process document. The companion emits this when the user describes or refines their process. During alpha every mutate_document is pended for human confirmation regardless of the confirmation field.

path.description: File path relative to workspace root, e.g. simops/process.yaml

patch.description: The patch to apply. Shape is app-specific; for SimOps this is a partial ProcessConfig.

content.description: Full serialised document content after applying the patch. Required for auto-apply; optional for ask.

rationale.description: Why this change is being made. Shown in the diff modal.

confirmation.description: auto = apply immediately; ask = pend for human review. Alpha: always treated as ask.

app_schema.description: App schema slug — kask_simops for SimOps.

response.action_id: UUID of the created action log entry
response.path: the file path that was (or will be) written

action_types.description: Create a named variant of the canonical process by applying a patch over a source state. Written to simops/variations/<slug>.yaml in the workspace git.

name.description: Human-readable variation name, e.g. CO2 capture @ 75%

patch.description: What differs from the source — partial ProcessConfig

hypothesis.description: What you expect this variation to achieve and why

response.action_id: UUID of the action log entry

action_types.description: Record a comparison request across named variants. The server records the intent; the client dispatches the cascade runs and narration, then calls /accept with the results.

variants.description: List of variant slugs to compare, e.g. ["base", "co2-capture-75"]

narrate_via.description: Agent to narrate results, e.g. comparator

response.action_id: UUID — pass to /accept with results once cascades complete

action_types.description: Record a member agent invocation in the action log. Actual execution is via workspace messages or MCP execute_agent — this is the audit record.

agent_id.description: Agent to invoke, e.g. simops_cascade, supply_chain_oracle

query.description: Structured query — object or string, agent-specific

response.action_id: UUID of the action log entry

action_types.description: Declare what kind of sensor or data source can supply a process field. This is how the Sensor Bridge knows what a field expects and how to bind live data to it.

stage_id.description: Stage ID this contract applies to, e.g. fermentation

field.description: Field name, e.g. efficiency, carbon_intensity, sidestream.co2.capture_fraction

observable_property.description: SOSA-style observable property name in snake_case, e.g. yield_fraction

unit.description: UCUM-style unit, e.g. dimensionless, kg, L, Cel

response.action_id: UUID of the action log entry

action_types.description: Record a typed observation about the process, a stage, or a variation. Stored in workspace_annotations for querying and resolving. Shown inline near the target in the UI.
action_types.cli: abw workspace actions annotate <ws-id> "body text" --kind insight --target stage:fermentation

kind.description: critique = something looks wrong; insight = non-obvious observation; risk = downside to flag; decision = recorded choice

target.description: What this applies to: stage:<id> | process | variation:<slug>

severity.description: info = grey; warn = amber; block = red (reserve for model-breaking issues)

response.action_id: UUID of the action log entry

parsing.description: How to extract action blocks from a companion response
parsing.algorithm: Split on __ACTION__\n...\n__END_ACTION__ — each block contains a single JSON object. Everything outside the delimiters is prose for the user.

type_name_map.description: SimOps companion uses domain-specific aliases in its prompt. Map to canonical API type names when posting to action endpoints.
